title: Impact of Overtime Eligibility Expansion on Work Hours

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two periods (pre/post) and two groups (newly overtime-eligible treated vs ineligible controls). We estimate y = log(hours) on treated, post, and their interaction; the interaction coefficient is the DID estimate of the policy’s causal effect on hours for the treated.
- Why: The policy change is plausibly exogenous, and we have treated/control groups observed before and after the change. DID isolates the differential post-period change for treated relative to controls.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the policy, treated and control groups would have experienced the same change in log hours over time.
  - No spillovers/interference: Control units are not indirectly affected by the policy (SUTVA).
  - No anticipation: Behavior did not change prior to the post indicator.
  - Stable composition: The treated/control group composition is stable across periods (or selection is not differentially changing in a way that affects trends).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(lmtest)
  library(sandwich)
})

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s32_data.csv"
dat <- readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2) Basic checks and ensure interaction is correct
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    treated = as.integer(treated),
    post = as.integer(post),
    treat_x_post_calc = treated * post
  )

# If provided treat_x_post mismatches, overwrite with the correct interaction
mismatch_n <- sum(dat$treat_x_post != dat$treat_x_post_calc, na.rm = TRUE)
if (mismatch_n > 0) {
  warning(sprintf("Found %d mismatches in treat_x_post; recomputing as treated*post.", mismatch_n))
  dat <- dat %>% mutate(treat_x_post = treat_x_post_calc)
}

# 3) Main DID regression: y ~ treated + post + treated:post (via treat_x_post)
# Heteroskedasticity-robust (HC2) standard errors
m_main <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = dat)
vcov_hc2 <- sandwich::vcovHC(m_main, type = "HC2")
ct_main <- lmtest::coeftest(m_main, vcov. = vcov_hc2)

# Extract DID estimate and inference
beta <- unname(coef(m_main)["treat_x_post"])
se   <- sqrt(diag(vcov_hc2))["treat_x_post"]
tval <- beta / se
pval <- 2 * pt(-abs(tval), df = nrow(dat) - length(coef(m_main)))
ci_l <- beta - 1.96 * se
ci_u <- beta + 1.96 * se
pct  <- 100 * (exp(beta) - 1)  # percent change in hours

# 4) Robustness A: Alternative robust SE (HC3)
vcov_hc3 <- sandwich::vcovHC(m_main, type = "HC3")
se_hc3 <- sqrt(diag(vcov_hc3))["treat_x_post"]
ci_l_hc3 <- beta - 1.96 * se_hc3
ci_u_hc3 <- beta + 1.96 * se_hc3

# 5) Robustness B: Manual cell-means DID (sanity check)
cell_means <- dat %>%
  group_by(treated, post) %>%
  summarize(mean_y = mean(y, na.rm = TRUE), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

mt1 <- cell_means %>% filter(treated == 1 & post == 1) %>% pull(mean_y)
mt0 <- cell_means %>% filter(treated == 1 & post == 0) %>% pull(mean_y)
mc1 <- cell_means %>% filter(treated == 0 & post == 1) %>% pull(mean_y)
mc0 <- cell_means %>% filter(treated == 0 & post == 0) %>% pull(mean_y)
did_cell <- (mt1 - mt0) - (mc1 - mc0)

# 6) Robustness C: Median (quantile) DID for outlier-robustness (if available)
median_est <- NA_real_
median_pct <- NA_real_
rq_available <- requireNamespace("quantreg", quietly = TRUE)
if (rq_available) {
  rq_fit <- quantreg::rq(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = dat, tau = 0.5)
  median_est <- unname(coef(rq_fit)["treat_x_post"])
  median_pct <- 100 * (exp(median_est) - 1)
}

# 7) Print clear numerical results
cat("Difference-in-Differences (DID) estimate on log(hours):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Beta_hat (treat x post): %.4f\n", beta))
cat(sprintf("  Robust SE (HC2): %.4f\n", se))
cat(sprintf("  95%% CI (HC2): [%.4f, %.4f]\n", ci_l, ci_u))
cat(sprintf("  p-value (HC2): %.4f\n", pval))
cat(sprintf("  Implied percent change in hours: %.2f%%\n\n", pct))

cat("Robustness A: Alternative robust SE (HC3)\n")
cat(sprintf("  95%% CI (HC3): [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n", ci_l_hc3, ci_u_hc3))

cat("Robustness B: Manual cell-means DID (sanity check)\n")
cat(sprintf("  Cell-means DID (log points): %.4f\n", did_cell))
cat(sprintf("  Implied percent change: %.2f%%\n\n", 100 * (exp(did_cell) - 1)))

if (rq_available) {
  cat("Robustness C: Median DID (quantile regression, tau=0.5)\n")
  cat(sprintf("  Median DID (log points): %.4f\n", median_est))
  cat(sprintf("  Implied percent change: %.2f%%\n", median_pct))
} else {
  cat("Robustness C: quantreg package not available; median DID skipped.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Slightly negative or near zero. Expanding overtime eligibility raises employers’ marginal cost of overtime hours, which can reduce assigned hours or shift work across workers. For salaried employees newly covered, firms may curb hours rather than pay the premium.
- Magnitude: Small in log points, roughly -0.02 to -0.05 (about -2% to -5%) on hours, with modest precision given sample size. Any increase in hours (positive effect) would likely be small if substitution toward non-overtime or schedule re-optimization occurs.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log hours worked before and after the policy change between treated and untreated groups.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The expansion of overtime eligibility significantly increased the log hours worked.
